Finally, what does it mean to be “approximately normal?” Sometimes, data that are mound shaped but
not exactly normal may be good enough for the procedures we want to use. In other cases, the procedure
may be very sensitive to the normality assumption and give unreliable results if the data are not
normal. The procedures we present in chapters 8, 9, and 10 will work
even if the data are not “exactly normal.” In statistics, we say that the procedures are
of a robust process as one that is flexible and dependable even when the data are not exactly normal.
